stem: Ananya pulls a block on a smooth horizontal spring 4 cm to the right of its mean position and releases it. Later it is at x = +2 cm, moving right. What is true about the restoring force at that instant?

options.A: It points right, the same way the block is moving
options.B: It points left, toward the mean, and is half as large as at x = +4 cm
options.C: It points left, toward the mean, and is just as large as at x = +4 cm
options.D: It points right, away from the mean, and grows as the block moves out

r1.text: The block is going right, so the force has to be pushing it right, otherwise it wouldn't move that way.

r2.text: F = −kx, so the force is opposite to x, toward the mean, and at 2 cm it's half of what it is at 4 cm.

r3.text: It's the same spring with the same k, so the pull back is the same at every point.

steps.text: Direction: F = −kx, so at x = +2 cm the force points in −x, toward the mean, whichever way the block is moving.
steps.trap_text: thinking the force points the way the block is moving (right).
thinking the force is the same at every point because k is the same.

verify_flags: 'Later ... moving right' is valid: after release from +4 cm the block passes the mean, reaches −4 cm, and returns rightward through +2 cm on its way out to +4 cm

stem: At a Nashik fair, a small pendulum bob swings through small angles. Right now it is halfway between the lowest point and its right extreme, still moving right. Which describes the restoring force on it?

options.A: Toward the lowest point, and it will be twice as large at the extreme
options.B: Toward the lowest point, and the same size at every point of the swing
options.C: Along its motion, toward the right extreme
options.D: Zero, because the bob is not yet at the extreme

r1.text: The bob is moving right, so the force must be acting right along with it.

r2.text: Gravity is the same everywhere, so the pull back toward the bottom is the same at every point.

r3.text: For small swings the restoring force is proportional to displacement and points back to the bottom, so doubling the distance doubles it.

calc: Small angles: F ≈ −(mg/L)x, so |F| at x = A is twice |F| at x = A/2

steps.text: Direction: for small angles F ≈ −(mg/L)x, pointing back toward the lowest point, not along the motion.
steps.trap_text: thinking the force acts the way the bob is moving, toward the right extreme.

steps.text: Size: |F| ∝ x, so at the extreme (x = A) it is twice what it is at x = A/2.
steps.trap_text: thinking gravity's pull back is the same at every point of the swing.

verify_flags: Restoring force here means the tangential component of gravity; proportionality holds only for small angles (sin θ ≈ θ)

stem: At a Pune auto-parts lab, Kiran measures how the acceleration a (in m/s²) of four test mounts depends on displacement x (in m) from equilibrium. Which mount vibrates in SHM?

options.B: Mount 2: a has a fixed size of 2 m/s², always toward equilibrium

r1.text: SHM needs acceleration proportional to x and opposite to it, and −25x does that with ω = 5 rad/s.

r2.text: Acceleration should point the same way as the displacement, so a = +25x is the SHM one.

r3.text: As long as the push back is steady and toward equilibrium, it's SHM, so the fixed 2 m/s² one works.

calc: a = −ω²x with ω² = 25 s⁻² gives ω = 5 rad/s, T = 2π/5 ≈ 1.26 s

steps.text: SHM test: a = −ω²x, so a must point opposite to x, back toward equilibrium.
steps.trap_text: accepting a = +25x, where a points the same way as x, away from equilibrium.

steps.text: a must also grow in step with x: a fixed 2 m/s² doesn't, but a = −25x does (ω² = 25 s⁻², ω = 5 rad/s).
steps.trap_text: thinking any steady push back toward equilibrium gives SHM.

verify_flags: Mount 4 is periodic but not simple harmonic (a not proportional to x); Mount 2 oscillates but is not SHM

stem: A 0.5 kg block on a spring of force constant 50 N/m oscillates with amplitude 8 cm. What is its acceleration when it is 4 cm to the right (+x) of the mean position?

options.A: 8 m/s² toward the mean, the same as at every point
options.B: 4 m/s² to the right, away from the mean

r1.text: The acceleration is set by the amplitude, kA/m, and stays the same through the motion.

r2.text: ω² = k/m = 100, so a = −100 × 0.04 = −4 m/s², pointing back to the mean.

r3.text: The block is on the right side, so the acceleration also points right, away from the centre.

verify_flags: A uses ω²A = 100 × 0.08 = 8 m/s² (max value) for every point; C is the forgot-square slip ωx = 10 × 0.04 = 0.4

stem: Rohit's spring-block is at x = +3 cm and moving away from the mean position. In which direction does the restoring force on the block act? Give a reason.
answer_key: The restoring force acts toward the mean position, opposite to the displacement.
expected_reasoning: The restoring force is F = −kx, so it always opposes the displacement and points back to the mean, whichever way the block is moving; here it slows the block down.

follow_ups.S12: As the block moves from +3 cm out to the extreme, is it speeding up or slowing down, and what does that say about the force?
follow_ups.CORRECT_NO_REASON: Why does the force point that way even though the block is moving outward?
follow_ups.CORRECT: If a mount had a = +9x, would it oscillate about x = 0? Explain.
follow_ups.UNCLEAR: Can you describe the direction of the force relative to the mean position?

verify_flags: A correct answer like 'opposite to the direction of motion' contains the S12 phrase 'direction of motion'; engine should check accept_any before patterns or handle negation

stem: Ishaan pulls a spring-block 2 cm from the mean, then later 6 cm from the mean. Is the restoring force the same in both cases? Answer in one sentence with a reason.
answer_key: No, the restoring force at 6 cm is three times the force at 2 cm.
expected_reasoning: The restoring force is F = −kx, proportional to displacement, so tripling the displacement triples the force.

follow_ups.S11: If you stretch a spring a tiny bit and then a lot, does your hand feel the same pull both times?
follow_ups.CORRECT_NO_REASON: Why exactly three times, and not just 'more'?
follow_ups.CORRECT: If the force at 2 cm is 0.6 N, what is the force constant k, and what is the force at the mean position?
follow_ups.UNCLEAR: Is the force at 6 cm larger, smaller, or the same as at 2 cm, and by how much?

steps.text: Restoring force: F = −kx, so its size is proportional to the displacement.
steps.trap_text: thinking the force is the same at every displacement because it's the same spring.

steps.text: Compare: |F₆| ÷ |F₂| = 6/2 = 3, so the force at 6 cm is three times the force at 2 cm.
steps.trap_text: subtracting 6 − 2 instead of dividing, so missing that the force triples.

verify_flags: A student writing 'not the same in both' would also hit the S11 phrase 'same in both'; engine negation handling to check

stem: A 2 kg block on a spring of force constant 200 N/m is 5 cm from its mean position. Find the magnitude of its acceleration and say which way it points.
answer_key: The acceleration is 5 m/s², directed toward the mean position.
expected_reasoning: ω² = k/m = 100 s⁻², so |a| = ω²x = 100 × 0.05 = 5 m/s², and a = −ω²x points opposite to the displacement, toward the mean.

slips.why: forgot to square ω: used ωx = 10 × 0.05
gave the force kx = 200 × 0.05 instead of dividing by m
used x = 5 cm without converting to metres

follow_ups.S12: If the acceleration pointed away from the mean, would the block ever come back? What would happen to x?
follow_ups.S11: What would the acceleration be at 2.5 cm from the mean, and at the mean itself?
follow_ups.CORRECT_NO_REASON: How did you get that value, and why does it point that way?
follow_ups.CORRECT: If the amplitude is 10 cm, what is the maximum acceleration, and where does it occur?
follow_ups.UNCLEAR: Can you give the size of the acceleration with its unit, and its direction relative to the mean?

verify_flags: tolerance assumed relative (5%); confirm engine convention
